children: shares rose 12% in premarket trading on Tuesday after
reported that the healthcare software provider is exploring options, including a potential sale that could take the company private, two years after its New York listing.
The Lehi, Utah, and Louisville, Kentucky-based ​company has hired investment bank Evercore
to advise on the process, which is ⁠currently at an early stage, the report said, citing sources.

The plans could change and a sale may not materialize, they cautioned. Waystar's market value has fallen to roughly $4.8B after a 24% slide in its share price this year amid a broader selloff ​in the software sector.
An auction process could gauge whether investor appetite for software businesses is ​returning, the report added.

Investors initially embraced the story, helping drive the shares from $20 to a 2025 peak of $45, but the stock ​later came under pressure ​as investors grew concerned ⁠that advances in artificial intelligence could disrupt software companies, Morgan Stanley analysts said in a report in July.

Waystar was formed in a 2017 ​merger between healthcare revenue management companies Zirmed and Navicure. EQT remains the company's largest shareholder with a 13% stake, followed by CPPIB with 10% and ⁠BlackRock ​Institutional Trust Company
with 8%, the report said, citing LSEG data.

title: Waystar shares rise on potential take-private deal report
